source.title: NVC-1B: A Large Neural Video Coding Model
source.authors: Xi-Hua Sheng; Chuanbo Tang; Li Li; Dong Liu; Feng Wu

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some PDF text-extraction and figure-layout artifacts occur, but the document is not cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites scaling laws as motivation for enlarging a neural video codec and reports compression outcomes, but it does not test the claimed held-out language-model loss laws or fit power laws to its own results.
record.gate_note: The paper scales components of neural video coding models and measures video-compression performance, primarily BD-rate and PSNR. It does not measure held-out cross-entropy loss, training-token or compute scaling, extrapolation from small-run fits, or a compute-optimal allocation. Its video-codec results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version, not as tests of a claim version. Scaling-law results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Kaplan et al. as motivation and scales parts of a neural video codec. It reports only compression results (BD-rate, PSNR) for a handful of component sizes. It reports no held-out loss curve, no power-law fit, no token or compute axis, no extrapolation and no compute-optimal split. It therefore does not test V1–V7, including V5 for video. Its non-monotonic, component-dependent gains bear on a different claim about codec component scaling.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that scaling the contextual and temporal-context modules improves compression, while scaling the motion modules helps only slightly before gains fall. CNNs beat Transformer variants at similar size. Their 1.36B-parameter NVC-1B reaches −25.1% average RGB BD-rate vs VTM, against −12.7% for the 21M baseline. They make no claim about power-law scaling.
record.recipe_differences: The paper scales neural video-coding modules and evaluates rate-distortion performance; it does not use the original language-model loss-fitting method or measure parameter, token, or compute power laws.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported codec outcomes vary by module and architecture: enlarging motion encoder-decoder components can reduce performance gains, while enlarging contextual and temporal-context components is reported to improve them; Transformer-based alternatives perform worse than CNN counterparts in the stated comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: In a CNN neural video codec, enlarging the contextual encoder-decoder, contextual entropy model and temporal context mining module gives steady BD-rate gains. Enlarging the motion encoder-decoder past 52M lowers the gain (15.4% to 1.5% on HEVC Class C) and makes training less stable. At similar sizes, Transformer and mixed variants do worse than CNN counterparts or crash.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling parameter count in neural video codecs improves compression only for some components and architectures; gains are non-monotonic for motion coding modules.

record.problems: The reported component-scaling results use video-compression metrics rather than held-out cross-entropy loss and do not fit or test power laws. Several exploratory results are presented in figures; the text gives only selected numerical examples. The paper also reports that some enlarged-model training runs crash or become unstable.
record.rows_left_out: Other figure-only values from the component and architecture sweeps were not separately extracted because their mapping to individual models and outcomes is not sufficiently clear in the extracted figure layout. The paper's broader benchmark tables compare codecs but do not report scaling-law tests.

untested.parts: Held-out LM pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute; no power-law fit reported.
Extrapolation from small-run fits to larger runs.
Shape effects on LM loss at fixed parameter count. The CNN vs Transformer codec comparisons are architecture-family swaps in a video codec, not LM shape sweeps.
Whether a power-law form holds for video models. Only a few component sizes are scaled, measured by BD-rate, with no fit of any functional form.
Downstream predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted exponents or optimal split on setup and fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: Rows are correctly linked to 'none'. The Fig. 6 caption mislabels the Transformer models as M19–M21; the text identifies them as M22–M24, and the rows use the correct ids. All results are single runs with no uncertainty reported. Because training crashes affected several larger models, size effects are confounded with training stability.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power-law fits to smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation as a function of compute.
Effects of depth, width, and architecture on held-out language-model loss at fixed parameter count.
The paper studies video coding, but does not test whether power-law forms hold in that modality or report a power-law fit.
Predictability of downstream task performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted language-model scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocations on setup and fitting choices.

rows.subject: M1
rows.operation_detail: Scaled up the motion encoder-decoder from the 21M-parameter baseline.
rows.measure: Video-compression performance gain relative to the small baseline model.
rows.note: This is a video-compression result, not a held-out loss or power-law measurement.

rows.subject: M3
rows.operation_detail: Further increased the motion encoder-decoder size.
rows.measure: Video-compression performance gain relative to the small baseline model.
rows.note: The authors state that the gain falls as this module is enlarged further; this does not measure a power-law loss curve.

rows.subject: M4
rows.operation_detail: Scaled up the motion entropy model on the M1 model.
rows.measure: Video-compression performance gain relative to the small baseline model.
rows.baseline: 21M-parameter DCVC-SDD baseline; M1 result stated as 15.4%
rows.note: The stated result is a small additional codec-performance gain, not a loss-scaling measurement.

rows.subject: M9
rows.operation_detail: Scaled up the contextual encoder-decoder from the 21M-parameter baseline.
rows.measure: Video-compression performance gain relative to the small baseline model.
rows.note: The authors describe sustained gains for this codec component, not a power-law fit.

rows.subject: M12
rows.operation_detail: Scaled up the contextual entropy model on the M9 model.
rows.measure: Additional video-compression performance gain relative to M9.
rows.note: The reported measure is codec performance, not held-out loss.

rows.subject: M13
rows.operation_detail: Scaled up the temporal context mining module from the 21M-parameter baseline.
rows.measure: Video-compression performance gain relative to the small baseline model.
rows.note: The paper reports the endpoint value in its discussion of a size sweep.

rows.subject: M15
rows.operation_detail: Further scaled up the temporal context mining module from the 21M-parameter baseline.
rows.measure: Video-compression performance gain relative to the small baseline model.
rows.note: The paper reports the endpoint value in its discussion of a size sweep.

rows.subject: M12
rows.operation_detail: CNN-based model with a larger contextual encoder-decoder and contextual entropy model.

conditions.value: comparison with enlarged temporal context mining

rows.measure: Video-compression performance gain relative to the small baseline model.
rows.note: This is the comparison point for M18's added temporal-context-module scaling.

rows.subject: M18
rows.operation_detail: Further scaled the temporal context mining module on the M12 model.
rows.measure: Video-compression performance gain relative to the small baseline model.
rows.baseline: 21M-parameter DCVC-SDD baseline; M12 result stated as 14.2%
rows.note: The authors report an added gain from enlarging this component; no power-law loss is evaluated.

rows.subject: M12
rows.operation_detail: CNN-architecture counterpart compared with mixed CNN-Transformer M20.
rows.measure: Video-compression performance gain relative to the small baseline model.
rows.note: Included as a codec architecture comparison, not a language-model loss result.

rows.subject: M20
rows.operation_detail: Inserted SwinTransformer layers into the CNN-based contextual entropy model, on M19.
rows.measure: Video-compression performance gain relative to the small baseline model.
rows.baseline: 21M-parameter DCVC-SDD baseline; M12 CNN counterpart stated as 15.6%
rows.note: The text reports lower codec performance than the similarly sized CNN counterpart.

rows.subject: M21
rows.operation_detail: Inserted SwinTransformer layers into the temporal context mining module on M20.
rows.measure: Video-compression performance gain relative to the small baseline model.
rows.baseline: 21M-parameter DCVC-SDD baseline; M20 result stated as 9.4%
rows.note: The authors say this module's Transformer insertion reduces the codec-performance gain.

rows.subject: M22
rows.operation_detail: Replaced contextual encoder-decoder convolutional layers and residual blocks with SwinTransformer layers.
rows.measure: Video-compression performance relative to baseline and CNN counterpart.
rows.baseline: 21M-parameter DCVC-SDD baseline; CNN counterpart M7 (50M parameters)
rows.value: A little performance gain over the small baseline; much smaller gain than M7
rows.note: No numerical gain is stated in the text.

rows.subject: M23
rows.operation_detail: Replaced contextual entropy-model convolutional layers and depth blocks with SwinTransformer layers, on M22.
rows.measure: PSNR relative to the small baseline model.
rows.value: PSNR loss of more than 4dB; BD-rate difficult to calculate
rows.note: The model crashed, and the reported PSNR result is not a held-out language-model loss measurement.

rows.measure: PSNR relative to the small baseline model.
